title: Singlife Davao Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Singlife Davao Marathon 2026 Review: Heat, Pace, Rules
meta_description: Singlife Davao Marathon 2026 review: a midnight start at SM Lanang in 28°C air, the out-and-back course to the Coastal Road, cut-offs, aid, field depth and Kadayawan logistics.
dek: What it was like to run Davao City's marathon on 15 August 2026: the midnight start, the humid night air, the course and rules, how fast the field ran, and racing on Kadayawan weekend.
verdict: Enter if you are a Filipino club runner chasing a place, or want a certified marathon on a festival weekend. The 2026 race drew about 3,000 runners, but only 568 finished the marathon, so 3:29 put a woman in the overall top ten and 3:49 made the Filipino women's paid top ten. Water and sports drinks came every 2 to 2.5 km, and the marathon limit was eight hours. The catch is the heat: at the midnight start it was 28°C with a 25°C dew point, and it never cooled below 27°C. Pace for that, and book a room early, because the race falls on Kadayawan weekend.

sections.heading: The Course: Out and Back to the Coastal Road
paragraphs: All four races start and finish at SM Lanang [1]. The marathon heads out along Cabaguio Avenue, Leon Garcia Street and Quezon Boulevard to the Davao City Coastal Road, then turns back for the finish [1]; the race report describes it as an out-and-back course [2]. The half marathon also uses part of the coastal road, the 10 km reaches Quezon Boulevard, and the 5 km stays on Cabaguio Avenue [1].

RunRio's chief executive, Rio dela Cruz, said the course was measured by an AIMS measurer from Malaysia, has World Athletics certification and is sanctioned by the Philippine Athletics Track and Field Association (Patafa) [1]. He said that lets times run here count for records and support some qualifying standards, subject to the rules [1].

No route map was published on the race pages. The rules still say the official marathon map 'will be announced soon' [3]. The FAQ said parts of the route would be closed on race day and pointed runners to the race and city traffic advisories [4].

sections.heading: Start Times, Time Limits and Aid
paragraphs: The marathon started at midnight, at the very start of Saturday 15 August [5][6]. The series website listed the other starts as 2am for the half marathon, 4.30am for the 10 km and 5.30am for the 5 km [5], but the timing data point to 3am, 4am and 5am [6]. Runners who did not start within 15 minutes of their flag-off were to be disqualified [3], so go by the race-week schedule rather than the website.

The series website gave time limits of eight hours for the marathon, four for the half, two for the 10 km and one for the 5 km [5]. Forty marathoners took more than seven hours, and the results list three who finished just past eight hours, at 8:02:47 to 8:02:50, as well as two half marathoners over four hours [6].

The rules promised a hydration station every 2 to 2.5 km with water and sports drinks, bananas on the longer races, and medics along the route and at the start and finish [3]. The organisers also promised pacers on the marathon and timing checkpoints every 5 km to flag incomplete results [1]. Top finishers are ranked on gun time [3].
Every finisher got a medal, towel and drawstring bag; only half and full marathon finishers got a finisher shirt [4].

sections.heading: The Weather: 28°C at Midnight, and It Never Cooled
paragraphs: Davao's Francisco Bangoy airport, about 3 km north-north-east of the start, recorded 28°C at midnight on race morning, with a dew point of 25°C, 84% humidity and a 4-knot wind [7]. It stayed at 28°C until 3am, dipped only to 27°C and 89% humidity from 4am to 6am, when the air was calm, and was back to 28°C at 7am. By 8am, when the eight-hour marathon limit ran out, it was 30°C [7].

A dew point of 25°C is about as humid as runners meet: sweat barely evaporates, so the body sheds heat slowly the whole way. The median marathoner took 5:29:42 [6], which from a midnight start means finishing around 5.30am in 27°C air [7]. The three slowest finishers came in just after 8am, at 30°C [6][7]. Start well inside your flat-course pace and drink at every station.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The organiser put the turnout at around 3,000 runners [8], short of the 4,000 to 6,000 it had aimed for [1]. The results list 2,382 finishers: 568 in the marathon, 745 in the half, 632 in the 10 km and 437 in the 5 km [6]. The marathon field was 426 men and 139 women, and apart from 11 Kenyans and one Japanese runner, everyone in it was Filipino [6].

Kenyans took the top of the marathon. Victor Kipkemei Chepkwony won in 2:25:37 from David Kipkorir Rono (2:26:43) and Gilbert Cheruyot Muge (2:29:27), and Ziporah Wanjiru Kingori won the women's race in 2:49:50 from Pamela Chepkoech Bundotich (2:59:35) [6]. The Filipino titles went to Edsel Moral in 2:33:52 and to Christine Hallasgo, a Tokyo Olympian, in 3:03:16, third woman overall [2][8][6].

Behind them the field thins fast. Tenth place overall was 2:41:38 for men and 3:29:01 for women [6]. Filipino citizens have their own prize list, paid ten deep in the marathon and half marathon with no qualifying time [9]; the tenth Filipino man ran 2:53:45 and the tenth Filipina 3:49:11 [6]. International runners are paid only to fifth, and only inside 2:45 for men or 3:15 for women [10]; four of the five Kenyan women were inside that standard [6]. Each race in the series carries about ₱1.2 million in prizes [1].

Only 61 marathoners broke four hours, and 19 broke three [6]. Age groups are worth racing too: the top finishers in each marathon age group earn a guaranteed entry to the TCS Sydney Marathon, though they still pay its fees [4].
The half marathon was won in 1:09:56 by Corsino Satinitigan and in 1:29:20 by Afjeel Clampiano, and its median finisher took 2:42:32. The 10 km was won in 31:48 [6].

sections.heading: Race Weekend: Kadayawan in Full Swing
paragraphs: RunRio set the race on the eve of the culmination of Kadayawan on purpose, to give visitors what dela Cruz called the city's biggest festival [1]. Malacañang made Friday 14 August a special non-working holiday in Davao City for the Great Kadayawan Weekend of 14 to 16 August [11], and the festival closed with the Pamulak and Indak-Indak parade and grand showdown on Sunday 16 August [12]. The city tourism office expected 250,000 visitors, up from 206,506 in 2025 [12][11].

Sort out a room first. The organisers said they had partnered with hotels for discounted rates [1]. Race packs were collected on 13 and 14 August, 11am to 7pm, on showing the confirmation email and a valid ID; someone else could collect with an authorisation letter, and delivery was offered [4].

Regular entry cost ₱1,635 for the 5 km, ₱1,835 for the 10 km, ₱2,635 for the half and ₱3,035 for the marathon [1]; the marathon ran from ₱2,635 early to ₱3,535 late, with processing and web fees on top [3][4]. Entries cannot be refunded, deferred or transferred, and a bib swap means disqualification and suspension from future events [3]. The half and full marathon are for runners aged 18 and over [3]. Every registered runner got accident and life insurance of about ₱50,000, covering the periods before and after the race as well [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: Yes, if you are a Filipino runner who can run about 3:50 as a woman or 2:55 as a man: the prize list is ten deep and the field is small. It also suits anyone collecting the Philippine Marathon Majors, which can be completed over several years [1], and runners who want a certified course for a qualifying time [1].
Think twice if you race badly in heat, if a start at midnight on Friday night does not suit you, or if you want to study a route map before you enter.
No date, route map or start times for the next race had been published when this was written. Check the start times in the race-week notice, because in 2026 they differed from the series website.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race pages and rules, the full results, airport weather records and Philippine press reports.

faqs.question: What time does the Singlife Davao Marathon start?
faqs.answer: At midnight for the marathon. In 2026 it started at 12am on Saturday 15 August from SM Lanang. The timing data point to 3am for the half marathon, 4am for the 10 km and 5am for the 5 km, although the series website listed 2am, 4.30am and 5.30am, so check the race-week schedule.

faqs.question: How hot is the Singlife Davao Marathon?
faqs.answer: Hot and humid all night. At the midnight start in 2026, Davao airport recorded 28°C, a 25°C dew point and 84% humidity, with almost no wind. The lowest reading was 27°C, from 4am to 6am, and it was 30°C by 8am, when the eight-hour marathon limit ran out.

faqs.question: What is the time limit at the Singlife Davao Marathon?
faqs.answer: Eight hours for the marathon, according to the series website, with four hours for the half marathon, two for the 10 km and one for the 5 km. In 2026 the results still list three marathoners who finished just after eight hours and two half marathoners who took more than four.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to win prize money at the Singlife Davao Marathon?
faqs.answer: Filipino runners are paid ten deep in the marathon and half marathon, with no qualifying time. In 2026 the tenth Filipino man ran 2:53:45 and the tenth Filipina 3:49:11. International runners are paid only to fifth, and only inside 2:45 for men or 3:15 for women.

faqs.question: Is the Singlife Davao Marathon held during Kadayawan?
faqs.answer: Yes, on purpose. In 2026 it was run on Saturday 15 August, during the Great Kadayawan Weekend of 14 to 16 August and the day before the festival's closing Pamulak and Indak-Indak parade. The city expected 250,000 festival visitors, so book early; organisers partnered with hotels for discounted rates.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the template, about the race run on 15 August 2026. Weather is from airport METAR observations at Davao (RPMD), not a forecast. Results were read from Race Roster's public results data; start times for the 21 km, 10 km and 5 km are inferred from the timing data and differ from the times listed on the series website, which also shows the wrong date (16 August). The organiser's figure of about 3,000 runners and the 2,382 finishers in the results are both given. Organiza's first name follows the results (Ricky), not the press (Rick). No route map was published; a Manila Bulletin launch article with a fuller route description could not be read (HTTP 403), so it is not used. No first-hand runner account of the 2026 race was found. No rating.
